title: Hosted API request-window skew diagnostic and runbook draft
content:
Summary:

On 2026-06-17 between ~03:42 and 04:25 UTC we observed a high-severity degradation of the Hosted API affecting streaming responses and TTFB for a subset of customers. Symptoms included elevated p50/p95 TTFB, partial streaming stalls (clients saw long pauses between tokens), and ~1.2% 5xx spike concentrated on edge proxies routing to a narrow set of backends. Impacted traffic: ~8% of global requests, skewed to EU and US-west. Duration: ~43 minutes of elevated errors/latency with residual elevated TTFB for next 2 hours. PagerDuty alerts fired and oncall routed a two-person SRE + runtime engineer team.

Immediate mitigation:
- At 03:55 UTC we enabled temporary routing fallback to the FallbackModelVariant cluster for streaming routes which reduced observed streaming stalls by ~70% within 6 minutes.
- At 04:10 UTC a conservative kv-cache eviction parameter rollback (reverting a recently-deployed timing change) reduced 5xx rate to baseline and normalized kv lock contention metrics.

Customer impact:
- ~8% of request volume saw degraded streaming behavior and elevated latency.
- Several paid customers reported degraded user experience; CS triaged and logged incidents for three enterprise tenants with partial failures.

Detection and initial triage (notes):
- First signal: increase in TTFB p50 from 180ms to 450ms observed on synthetic/dogfood monitors at 03:43 UTC.
- Secondary signals: surge in HTTP response code 502/504 from edge region eu-west-1 and us-west-2; spike in streaming session stalls in streaming trace histogram.
- Telemetry: KV-cache lock wait time (kvcache.lock_wait_ms.p95) increased by 6x; per-backend CPU utilization stayed flat.
- Hypothesis formed quickly: a scheduling/timing regression changed kvcache scrub/eviction timing leading to transient lock amplification and request window skew.

Timeline (reconstructed from traces, logs, and deploy history):
- 2026-06-17 03:30 UTC: Rollout of runtime patch rrt-2026-06-17-003 (small scheduler/timer change to kvcache scrub) begins to 10% canary (internal).
- 03:41 UTC: Synthetic monitors detect p50 TTFB increase; alerts threshold crossed and PD triggered (page: oncall-sre).
- 03:42-03:47 UTC: SRE oncall pulls up traces; consistent pattern: requests processed by a small number of backends show growing kv lock wait times; streaming 'resume' packets delayed.
- 03:50 UTC: Identified that canary backends were in the same maintenance window and that the scheduler change increased scrub alignment across instances (more synchronized evictions).
- 03:55 UTC: Routing fallback to FallbackModelVariant applied for streaming endpoints (config change via edge router). Immediate partial recovery.
- 04:02 UTC: Investigated the new scheduler config; rolled back the change in canary pool (manual rollback of rrt-2026-06-17-003) to mitigate synchronized kv scrub.
- 04:10 UTC: Rollback complete; kv lock wait metrics trending back to baseline; 5xx counts normalized.
- 04:25 UTC: PD resolved (alerts suppressed), monitoring remained for 2 hours.

Root cause analysis (working):
Primary cause: a timing/scheduling change introduced in rrt-2026-06-17-003 altered the kv-cache scrub interval alignment across instances, producing a highly-correlated eviction wave. The correlated evictions increased contention on kv locks, which amplified request window skew: streaming requests that rely on incremental KV-prefetch/resume saw token emission pauses when the KV subsystem transiently thrashed.

Contributing factors:
- The canary rollout was to a small set of instances colocated in the same maintenance schedule/host pool -> reduced diversity and made correlated behavior likely.
- Lack of a direct synthetic against kv lock wait (we watched TTFB & streaming histograms but had no guardrail threshold on kvcache.lock_wait_ms).
- The scheduler change was small and passed unit tests; integration load test did not reproduce timing alignment at the same scale because it randomized instance start times.
- Runtime telemetry sampling rates for detailed streaming resumes were low for high-throughput routes, which delayed precise symptom diagnosis.

Evidence collected:
- Traces: 250+ APM traces showing token emission gap aligned with spikes in kvcache.lock_wait_ms on the same host IDs.
- Logs: recent deploy metadata shows rrt-2026-06-17-003 applied to canary-hosts X,Y,Z at 03:30 UTC.
- Metrics: kvcache.lock_wait_ms.p95 spiked from ~4ms to ~28ms for the canary pool during the window. Edge 502/504s map to time windows of elevated kv lock wait.

Why the rollback worked:
- Reverting the scheduler/timer change restored staggered eviction relative offsets across instances; without the synchronized eviction wave, lock contention reduced and request window skew disappeared.

Runbook draft (playbook to detect & mitigate similar incidents):
- Monitoring/Alerting additions (short-term):
  - Add a dedicated alert for kvcache.lock_wait_ms.p95 exceeding 10ms sustained 3m across any backend pool.
  - Add streaming token-gap SLI (percentage of streaming responses with inter-token gap > 1s) and alert at 0.5% sustained 5m.
- Immediate oncall triage steps (flow):
  1. Observe which backend pools show elevated kvcache.lock_wait_ms. Query: "sum by(pool) (increase(kvcache_lock_wait_ms_bucket[1m]))" (approx).
  2. If the elevated pool corresponds to a recent rollout (check deploy metadata), and CPU is not saturated, assume timing/coordination regression; consider rollback for canary group.
  3. Apply routing fallback to FallbackModelVariant for streaming routes for the affected customers/regions. Note: use conservative config to avoid cascading capacity issues.
  4. Roll back the suspected runtime change from the canary group. Monitor kvcache metrics for return to baseline.
  5. If rollback not available or rollback fails, increase kv-cache shard count (if supported) or implement temporary rate-limiting on streaming routes to reduce contention while engineers craft a fix.
- Communication template (to use in PD/SRE -> CS/higher ops):
  - Short update: what we saw, regions affected, immediate mitigation applied, ETA for fix.
  - Post-incident: brief technical cause, customers affected, whether data/exposure occurred (no in this incident).

Post-incident action items (owner, due):
- A1: Add kvcache.lock_wait_ms alert and streaming token-gap SLI (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-06-24).
- A2: Patch the rollout tooling to avoid canary placement in the same maintenance pool (owner: Jordan Kim, due: 2026-06-30).
- A3: Add an integration test that can reproduce staggered-timer alignment (owner: Liam O'Connor, due: 2026-07-07).
- A4: Increase runtime telemetry sampling for streaming resume traces during canaries (owner: Ben Thompson, due: 2026-06-22).
- A5: Update the streaming runbook with the fallback and rollback flow and include explicit commands (owner: Marisol Reyes, due: 2026-06-21).

Open questions / things to verify:
- Why did integration load tests not catch the alignment? Need to inspect test harness start ordering and whether it seeds deterministic timers. TODO: reproduce locally.
- Is there a safe way to make kvcache eviction offsets randomized by default to avoid tight alignment across instances? (longer-term item for runtime team).
- Could autoscaler / placement changes inadvertently concentrate canaries? We should validate cluster tooling.

Retrospective notes (quick thoughts):
- Small scheduler/timer changes have outsized risk because they can change global coordination behaviors. We should treat changes to periodic background jobs as higher-risk and gate with additional canary diversity requirements.
- Runbook lacked an explicit query for kvcache lock wait; that slowed precise triage by ~6-8 minutes. Adding the alert will buy time.
- Communication: CS was informed within 25 minutes and sent templated messages; good work but we should add a short customer impact assessment checklist to be filled before external comms.

Appendix: quick diagnostic commands (work-in-progress)
- kvcache lock wait by host: "sum by(host) (rate(kvcache_lock_wait_ms_count[1m])) / sum by(host) (rate(kvcache_lock_wait_ms_sum[1m]))" (approx p95 proxy)
- identify recent deploys: "select * from deploys where tag ~ rrt-2026-06-17-003 and since 03:00"
- streaming gap traces: APM query "trace where event='stream_resume' and gap_ms > 500"

Notes to self / informal: 
- Keep this doc intentionally rough — want it editable by runbook editors and runtime.
- We should run a small chaos experiment to intentionally align eviction timers in staging and see if we can get reproducible lock amplification. Add as part of A3.
- Chat log: quick snippet from oncall at 03:56 (copied to linked_artifacts).

Status: draft. Will convert to final postmortem after action items closed and test reproductions confirmed.

-- end of doc --
